title: Redwood - Data Retention & PII Controls Demo - Zenith Financial
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Zenith through the Console and API controls for request logging, PII redaction, and retention policies. Customer emphasized regulatory needs (financial data, EU residency), desire for per-route control, and the ability to opt-out of storage for sensitive endpoints. Next steps: send SOC2 + security whitepaper, provide trial org with storage toggles enabled, run a short pilot to validate redaction and retention, schedule procurement follow-up.
action_items: Maya Chen | Share SOC 2, ISO and security whitepaper + KMS integration guide | 2026-03-06
Raj Patel | Provision trial org with demo tenant and per-route storage toggles enabled; upload sample prompt & results | 2026-03-09
Samir Desai | Provide sample request payloads (PII and non-PII) for redaction test | 2026-03-06
Erin Brooks | Confirm legal questions re: data residency and retention window | 2026-03-11
next_steps: Send security packet and KMS integration docs
Provision pilot environment and share access
Run redaction benchmark with customer payloads
Schedule procurement/contract sync in two weeks
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-04 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~45 minutes | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Raj (Redwood SE), Laura (Zenith CTO), Marco (DevOps), Erin (Legal), Samir (Engineer)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can start in a minute, Raj and I will walk through our data handling controls and the Console toggles, plus a quick API demo.
[00:12] Laura: Great, thanks. We're mostly concerned about PII leakage and retention because of EU customers and audits.
[00:20] Raj: Absolutely, we'll cover per-route storage, automatic PII detection and redaction, and how you can route sensitive traffic to a no-storage policy or to your private deployment via VPC.
[00:31] Marco: Quick Q up front - can we keep logs for 90 days for general telemetry but zero storage for payment-specific endpoints?
[00:40] Maya: Yes, that pattern is pretty common. You can set per-route retention windows; default might be 30/90/365, and you can set specific endpoints to never persist.
[00:52] Raj: I'll show the Console - there's a toggle on the route configuration: "store_requests" with options Off / Ephemeral / Persist. Ephemeral retains only in-memory for the duration of the inference and is not written to object storage.
[01:05] Marco: And where does the ephemeral data live - is it in our region or Redwood's control plane?
[01:12] Raj: Ephemeral is kept on the serving node's RAM and not persisted; for Private it's fully in-customer network. For hosted we run in region but never write to long-term storage when ephemeral is selected.
[01:24] Erin: On the legal side - we need audit logs that show who requested deletion and when. Do you have immutable audit trails?
[01:32] Maya: Yes, audit logs are separate from request storage. We maintain audit events by default (SAML events, admin changes), and they can be configured to be pushed to your SIEM. Those are metadata-level logs, not the request payloads.
[01:45] Raj: Ok starting demo - opening Console -> Projects -> Routes.
[01:54] Raj: Here on the route config you can toggle Request Storage: Off / Ephemeral / 30d / 90d / 1y. You can also enable Automatic Redaction Rules and upload a custom PII regex set.
[02:10] Raj: If you enable redaction, the system runs a PI EX model that tags PII and masks tokens before storing, also returns a redaction report. Note: the model is heuristics plus ML; you'll want to vet with sample payloads.
[02:26] Samir: Can we get the redaction metadata - like which spans were masked? We need it for debugging.
[02:33] Raj: Yes, redaction metadata is optional; you can choose to include a non-sensitive metadata-only report that lists spans and types (email, ssn-like, card) but that report can also be toggled off.
[02:45] Laura: Important for us is key management. If you store anything, we require CMEK via our KMS.
[02:52] Maya: That's supported - Redwood Private and Dedicated support CMEK via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations for on-prem. We'll share the KMS integration guide.
[03:03] Marco: For hosted API, what about encryption at rest and who has access to keys?
[03:08] Raj: By default Redwood-managed keys are used; with CMEK you control the key lifecycle. Access is restricted via RBAC and audit logs, and we provide key rotation patterns.
[03:18] Raj: Switching to API demo - here's a curl example to create a route and set "store_requests": "off" in the route template. (Shows curl)
[03:29] Raj: Note the policy param: "redaction: { mode: 'auto', includeMetadata: true }" or you can set mode: 'none' to skip redaction.
[03:40] Samir: If we set includeMetadata true, does that leak PII in the metadata?
[03:44] Raj: We strip actual token content from the metadata; metadata contains types and positions only, unless you explicitly choose to persist masked snippets for debugging.
[03:54] Marco: What about streaming responses - when streaming, is the payload sent to any logs?
[03:58] Raj: Streaming is handled in-memory, and we can set the streaming to be ephemeral as well. For persisted routes we persist the final output only if store_requests is set to a persistent option.
[04:10] Laura: We also have a compliance ask for residency - EU data must stay in eu-west. Can we pin region?
[04:16] Maya: Yes, region pinning plus private VPC ensures residency. For hosted we offer region selectors, and for Private you run wholly in your environment.
[04:25] Raj: Showing Optimize - it suggests retention profiles based on traffic patterns: high-traffic non-sensitive routes can be set to 30d, others to ephemeral. It shows estimated cost delta.
[04:38] Raj: Example: enabling ephemeral on a high-volume analytics route reduces storage costs by ~80% in our estimate.
[04:45] Erin: On deletions - if a user requests deletion under GDPR, can we delete all persisted requests for an identifier?
[04:52] Raj: Yes, we support subject access and deletion workflows. You can query by hashed identifiers and trigger bulk deletion; deletion events are recorded in the audit log. We can also configure automatic TTL-based purges.
[05:04] Samir: How deterministic is PII detection - any false positives that could mask useful debug info?
[05:10] Raj: There will be tradeoffs - the auto mode errs on the side of masking; we run evals and you can provide custom allow-lists and deny-lists. For debugging we recommend ephemeral with metadata enabled or short-term persistence like 7d.
[05:26] Marco: Are there SDK hooks to redact before sending, like a client-side sanitizer?
[05:31] Raj: Yes - we provide client libraries with pre-send hooks and wrappers for redaction and tokenization. Many customers use a hybrid approach: client-side redaction + server-side detection as fallback.
[05:41] Maya: Quick break for questions?
[05:43] Laura: On retention windows - will those windows appear in our contract/SLAs?
[05:48] Maya: For Dedicated/Private we can put retention in the contract; for hosted we offer policy-based guarantees and can include SLOs in enterprise agreements.
[05:56] Erin: For regulatory audits we will need provenance - who retrieved data and when. You said audit logs are separate, can they be exported to our SIEM?
[06:04] Raj: Yes, exports to CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Splunk/Elastic are supported. We also have webhooks for push delivery.
[06:12] Raj: Back to Console demo - creating a redaction profile: you can upload regexes, set model confidence thresholds, and choose to store only redaction masks.
[06:24] Samir: If we use custom regex, will that be applied pre or post model detection?
[06:28] Raj: You choose the order: regex-first (faster, deterministic) or model-first (captures more subtle PII). The UI warns about performance impacts.
[06:36] Marco: Any constraints on throughput when redaction is enabled? We're doing 2000 rps on some internal endpoints.
[06:42] Raj: For high throughput we recommend using our dedicated capacity and enabling batching; redaction adds CPU overhead. We can benchmark with your payloads; in Dedicated we can tune instances for higher throughput.
[06:55] Maya: I'll flag that as an action item to bench with Samir's sample requests.
[07:00] Laura: How do we handle logs for function/tool calling and structured outputs - do they store the original function args?
[07:06] Raj: Function/tool calls are treated like regular requests - you can strip or redact tool args via post-processing policies. We also support structured-output templates that only persist certain fields.
[07:18] Erin: For contracts we need indemnities around data breaches, is that handled at deal stage?
[07:23] Maya: Yes, legal teams negotiate those clauses; we provide SOC2 evidence and incident response docs. We'll connect legal to legal.
[07:32] Raj: Demoing API logs - here's a sample query against our request store (redacted) showing timestamps, route id, retention flag, and redaction metadata.
[07:44] Samir: Could you show a redaction report example?
[07:47] Raj: (Shows redaction report) It lists span offsets, types, confidence scores. See the confidence threshold slider - below 0.6 it won't mask by default if you choose conservative mode.
[08:00] Laura: What about PII in embeddings? We store embeddings for semantic search - is there a way to avoid embedding storage or to hash them?
[08:08] Raj: You can opt out of embedding persistence per-route or per-model. For hashed embeddings we offer deterministic hashing that prevents reconstruction; we can also push embeddings to your tenant storage via Private or S3 export.
[08:22] Marco: If we choose to store embeddings, can we enforce encryption with CMEK?
[08:25] Raj: Yes, CMEK covers embedding storage as well when configured.
[08:30] Maya: Recap - Redwood supports per-route storage toggles, automatic redaction (model + regex), optional redaction metadata, CMEK, audit log exports, region pinning, and pilot benchmarking.
[08:42] Laura: That covers most asks. Procurement timeline is about 4-6 weeks, but legal review will take time.
[08:48] Erin: We'll need the SOC2 and specific retention language. Also want an example contract clause for data residency.
[08:53] Maya: We'll send those.
[08:56] Raj: Quick note - Optimize can suggest retention configs based on traffic and cost; it can also simulate cost impact if you change retention windows.
[09:07] Samir: Last technical Q - can we automatically scrub PII from previously stored requests?
[09:11] Raj: Yes, we have a scrub API that can run deletes and masking over persisted store with a job id and audit log. It won't change immutable audit trails, but it will erase request payloads.
[09:22] Laura: Good. Ok, next steps then.
[09:25] Maya: Thanks everyone - we'll share the packet and spin up a demo tenant.
[09:28] Erin: Thanks, bye.
[09:30] End of meeting.

Notes about transcription: occasional misheard acronyms (PI EX instead of PII-X model) and speaker overlaps; timestamps approx every 15-60s to mimic Fireflies export.
